solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Purple loo with poster, not the first

parts.note: LAV is short for lavatory, a British word for loo

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the synonym for poster is dropped

parts.note: one who posts a letter is its sender

explanation.surface: A homeowner describes a purple toilet and the person who sent something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' cuts S from SENDER, leaving ENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a pale purple colour, named after the flower.

clue.text: Beer keeping one very animated

indicators.note: says the beer holds the other letters

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A beer containing something makes a drinker very lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Alive can mean lively and full of energy, as in 'alive with excitement'.

clue.text: Unusual kite etc, one not made of paper

indicators.note: suggests the letters of kite etc are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A strange kite made of something other than paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-ticket is an electronic travel or event ticket, with no paper version.

clue.text: Dull agent demanding payment

definitions.meaning: a ... is a debt collector, one who ...

explanation.surface: A tedious debt collector.
explanation.definitionFit: Dun has two senses: a drab brownish colour, and a person pressing for payment of a debt.

clue.text: Insubstantial fare I prepare roughly about start of Christmas

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters go round the next piece
indicates the letters of I prepare are arranged roughly, not in order
takes the first letter of Christmas

explanation.surface: A cook offers a meagre meal knocked together at the beginning of Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' turns I PREPARE into RIEPAPER, which goes 'about' C.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice paper is edible, very thin sheeting, hardly substantial food.

clue.text: Grass going back inside garden wall

indicators.note: tells us the hidden letters are read from right to left
says the answer sits within the words garden wall

explanation.surface: Grass is creeping back through the garden wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' finds NWAL across 'garden wall'; 'going back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is a stretch of mown grass in a garden.

clue.text: Word of apology, large, not small, one's articulated?

indicators.note: large, not small says one size letter replaces the other

parts.note: sorry is said to apologise

explanation.surface: Apologising in a big, not little, way: perhaps uttering words clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large, not small' swaps S for L in SORRY.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulated lorry is a large truck with a hinged joint between cab and trailer.

clue.text: Boy is going to India in the morning

parts.note: will expresses the future, as is going to does
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A lad plans to travel to India early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: William is a common male first name, so it can stand for a boy.

clue.text: Sight of German — is one inside?

indicators.note: signals that is plus one goes within the German word

parts.note: von is German for 'of', as in aristocratic names
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a German's eyesight is internal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal; the German word for 'of' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is the faculty of seeing, i.e. eyesight.

clue.text: Not exactly a part for a girl

parts.note: CA, circa, means approximately, i.e. not exactly
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An imprecise description of a role written for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Carole is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Odd bits of beefcake seen in Northern stream

indicators.note: points to the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of beefcake

explanation.surface: Fragments of a muscleman glimpsed in a stream up north.
explanation.walkthrough: A beck is a brook in Northern England dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Beck is the word used in northern England for a small stream or brook.

clue.text: Team coming in has pay altered: that's breathtaking!

indicators.note: says the team's letters enter the rearranged words
tells us the letters of has pay are to be rearranged

parts.note: XI is eleven, a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: A football side hears its wages have changed, to gasps of amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathtaking' is literal: asphyxia stops the breath. 'altered' gives ASPHYA, and the eleven is 'coming in' near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphyxia is suffocation, quite literally something that takes your breath away.

clue.text: Hateful injury to the person, or tear

parts.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, a British criminal offence of personal injury
taken as written
a rent is a rip or tear

explanation.surface: Something repugnant: either physical harm or a rip.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British legal term for an assault causing injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means detestable, inspiring loathing.

clue.text: Set to be in church

parts.note: the letter B is pronounced 'be', as in '2B or not 2B'
to be at home is to be in, so at can mean in

explanation.surface: An instruction that something is due to take place in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a set of things produced or dealt with together.

clue.text: Hairstyle for busy people?

definitions.meaning: a tall dome-shaped hairdo from the 1960s
figuratively a place full of busy workers, busy as bees

explanation.surface: A hairdo suited to people who are always rushing about.
explanation.definitionFit: A beehive is both a piled-up 1960s hairdo and a hive full of busy bees.

clue.text: Briefly sample new sacred song

indicators.note: says the shortened letters are made into something new, rearranged
means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Advice to try a quick taste of a fresh hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Agony as Dicky hugs Ian

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Dicky embraces Ian to his great distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but means shaky, signalling the letters of HUGS IAN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering, a synonym of agony.

clue.text: I might need a ruler, me — a certain king?

parts.note: taken as written
certain means sure
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch wonders whether someone sure of himself needs a ruler over him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who measures lengths would reach for a ruler, the straight-edged measuring tool.

clue.text: American saloon re-used anisette bottles

indicators.note: means the words hold the answer within them, as a bottle holds its contents

explanation.surface: A US bar recycles its bottles of anise liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' looks like a bar, but here it is a car: an American sedan is a British saloon car.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedan is the American word for what the British call a saloon car.

clue.text: Breathe in sharply when embraced by doctor

indicators.note: places one piece inside the doctor's letters

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A patient inhales suddenly on being hugged by a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to take a quick, sudden intake of air.

clue.text: Hard quality that's appropriate when speaking?

indicators.note: says the word for appropriate is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to appropriate something is to steal it

explanation.surface: A firmness of character that is fitting when talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb, meaning take.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is resolve or toughness, a hard quality of character, as in 'nerves of steel'.

clue.text: Remove coarser elements from puzzle

definitions.meaning: to pass soil or gravel through a sieve

explanation.surface: Sifting out the hard parts of a brainteaser.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddle has two senses: a coarse sieve or sifting, and an enigma posed as a question.

clue.text: Hang around, at first, looking on in the extreme rear

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Lurking about, watching from far at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly somewhere without obvious purpose.

clue.text: Behold, start of week makes you depressed

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: takes the first letter of week

explanation.surface: Look, Monday morning makes you miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel low is to be downhearted or in poor spirits.

clue.text: Boy is without a pulse

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the boy surrounds the letter

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad has no heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes, and a bean is one of them.

clue.text: Time to have everything including hospital and municipal building

indicators.note: places a letter within the run of letters before it

parts.note: to own something is to have it
all means everything
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A council claims it has time for everything, a hospital included.
explanation.definitionFit: A town hall houses local government offices, a civic building.
